review_notes: Reviewed all 58 lines of the target and read the relevant definitions and uses in PlanarAlgebra, PlanarGinibre, PositiveKernel, and FerromagneticMean, as well as the underlying Mathlib AddCircle/Circle and Real.Angle simp lemmas. The file has only one concrete simp-interface gap I can support: the zero case of planar_reference_mean_nonneg unfolds planarCos/planarCharacter instead of using a canonical zero lemma. I did not flag planarCos_add_antipode for simp annotation because it is a conditional identity with a single in-file use and explicit rewriting is already adequate. findings.problem: The equal-endpoint branch is closed by unfolding planarEnergy, planarCos, and planarCharacter all the way to the underlying AddCircle.toCircle and Complex.re definitions. The desired normal form is simply planarCos 0 = 1. Because planarCos is defined as (planarCharacter t).re and planarCharacter as AddCircle.toCircle t, and no [simp] zero lemma is exported for either wrapper, users have no direct way to simplify planarCos 0; the full unfolding at line 29 is a workaround and is brittle against changes to those definition bodies.
findings.proposed_change:
Add canonical evaluation lemmas in PlanarAlgebra, where the wrappers are defined:

  @[simp] theorem planarCos_zero : planarCos 0 = 1 := by
    simp [planarCos, planarCharacter]

  @[simp] theorem planarSin_zero : planarSin 0 = 0 := by
    simp [planarSin, planarCharacter]

Then replace the line-29 branch with `simp [planarEnergy, h]`, which reduces the zero difference to planarCos 0 and uses the new lemma. The exact replacement should be checked by Lean, but the lemma itself has no hypotheses and is a terminating ground evaluation.
findings.benefit: This gives planarCos the same canonical zero normal form that Mathlib provides for the underlying AddCircle.toCircle and Real.Angle cos, removes dependence on unfolding definition bodies in this proof, and makes the normal form reusable by other files that manipulate planarCos 0.
